title: Severe headache in pregnancy
guidance_text: Severe or persistent headache during pregnancy is a danger sign. Ask about visual symptoms and blood pressure, and arrange urgent review if danger signs are present.

title: Blurred vision in pregnancy
guidance_text: Blurred vision or other visual symptoms in pregnancy can indicate a danger sign, especially with headache or high blood pressure. Escalate for same-day clinical assessment.

title: High blood pressure in pregnancy
guidance_text: Elevated blood pressure in pregnancy with headache, visual symptoms, swelling, or abdominal pain requires urgent referral support and supervisor notification.

title: Reduced fetal movement
guidance_text: Reduced or absent fetal movement reported by a pregnant patient should be treated as a danger sign and referred for clinical assessment.

title: Vaginal bleeding during pregnancy
guidance_text: Any vaginal bleeding during pregnancy should be escalated for urgent clinical assessment. Do not delay referral while documenting.

title: Convulsions in pregnancy
guidance_text: Convulsions or seizures in pregnancy require immediate emergency referral and supervisor notification.

title: Severe abdominal pain
guidance_text: Severe abdominal pain during pregnancy is a danger sign. Arrange urgent assessment and document associated bleeding, fever, or fetal movement changes.

title: Fever in pregnancy
guidance_text: Fever in pregnancy requires assessment for infection and follow-up. Urgency increases when fever is severe or combined with abdominal pain, bleeding, or weakness.

title: Swelling of face or hands
guidance_text: Swelling of the face or hands during pregnancy can be a danger sign, especially with headache, visual symptoms, or high blood pressure.

title: Same-day referral guidance
guidance_text: When danger signs are present, support same-day referral to the nearest PHC or obstetric referral facility, notify the supervisor, and document CHW confirmation.
